stem: Four hyperbolas of the form $y=\frac{a}{x}$ are drawn on the same set of axes. Which one lies {=where} the axes?
solution: Only the size $|a|$ decides how far a hyperbola lies from the axes: the bigger $|a|$ is, the further the graph lies from the axes. The sign of $a$ only decides which quadrants the graph lies in.
Ignoring the signs, the sizes of $a$ in the four equations are ${=mag[0]}$, ${=mag[1]}$, ${=mag[2]}$ and ${=mag[3]}$.

The {=word} size is ${=mag[pc]}$, so the graph that lies {=where} the axes is $y={=sgl[pc]}\frac{{=nml[pc]}}{{=dnl[pc]}x}$. A negative $a$ is not a small $a$: it only puts the graph in the second and fourth quadrants.

proposed_misconceptions.label: A negative a is treated as a small a
proposed_misconceptions.description: The student compares the values of a with their signs, so a negative a (for example -6) is taken as smaller than a positive a (for example 2), instead of comparing the sizes |a| to decide how far the graph lies from the axes.

notes: The twist the book uses in exercise 6.8 question 20: a negative a and an a written as a unit fraction, y = -1/(2x). Four equations, written as a/x or as 1/(kx) with k = 2, 3 or 4, with mixed signs; the student must rank by |a|. Magnitudes are four distinct values drawn from 1/4, 1/3, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, ..., 9, so the four options always differ. Each option has its own reason: the right size; the opposite size (bigger-a-closer-to-axes); the one a student gets by ranking signed values (negative-a-taken-as-small), which the require keeps different from the other two; and a plain fourth. The stem only changes between closest and furthest, so distinct_by_choices is set.
